record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Given a strictly proper rational discrete-time SISO transfer function G(z), if every minimal positive realization may require adding extra eigenvalues beyond the poles of G(z), which additional eigenvalues can occur? Equivalently, can one fully characterize the possible "hidden modes" that must be introduced in order to obtain a minimal positive realization, and explain how those extra modes determine the minimal achievable order?

evidence.quote: Another important issue related to minimality of positive systems is the study of "hidden modes", i.e. of the eigenvalues which possibly one has to add in order to obtain a minimal positive realization.
A full characterization of this property may lead to a deeper and valuable insight into the problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G(z)$ be a strictly proper rational discrete-time single-input single-output transfer function with nonnegative impulse response, written in lowest terms as $G(z)=p(z)/q(z)$, and let $n=\deg q$ be the McMillan degree of $G$. A positive realization of $G$ is a triple $(A,b,c)$ with $A\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{N\times N}$, $b\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{N\times 1}$, $c\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{1\times N}$ (entries nonnegative) such that $G(z)=c(zI-A)^{-1}b$. The minimal positive realization dimension $N^{*}(G)$ is the smallest $N$ for which such a positive realization exists; in general $N^{*}(G)\ge n$, and the spectrum of $A$ in a minimal positive realization may contain eigenvalues that are not poles of $G(z)$ (so-called "hidden modes," i.e., eigenvalues $\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(A)\setminus\{\text{poles of }G\}$).

Provide a complete characterization of the set of possible hidden modes that can or must arise in a minimal positive realization of a given $G(z)$. Specifically:
(a) For each strictly proper $G(z)$ with nonnegative impulse response, describe the set of multisets $S\subset\mathbb{C}$ of complex numbers (with multiplicities) such that there exists a minimal positive realization $(A,b,c)$ in which $\operatorname{spec}(A)$ equals the poles of $G$ (with their multiplicities) together with $S$.
(b) Express $N^{*}(G)$ as $n+|S^{*}|$, where $S^{*}$ is a minimum-cardinality such multiset, and characterize $|S^{*}|$ in terms of structural data of $G$ (poles, residues, dominant pole, etc.).
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization of "hidden modes" and of the minimal positive realization dimension for an arbitrary strictly proper SISO transfer function with nonnegative impulse response is still open. Complete answers are known only in special cases (e.g., transfer functions with positive real poles, nonnegative multiple poles, or two-different-pole systems), but no general necessary-and-sufficient characterization is available. Recent surveys reiterate that minimality of positive realizations and the structure of required extra modes remain unresolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Positive Realizations of Transfer Functions With Real Poles
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses minimal positive realizations specifically in the real-poles case.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases (e.g., real poles) have known characterizations of minimality.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on minimal positive realizations summarizing open problems including hidden modes.
status_evidence.claim: Hidden modes and full characterization of minimal positive realization order remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations for linear systems with two-different-pole transfer functions
status_evidence.snippet: Provides minimal positive realizations only for the restricted case of two distinct poles.
status_evidence.claim: Progress is limited to restricted pole configurations; general case remains open.
